payload.title: Ideal rack-and-pinion motion conversion

model.title: Ideal rack-and-pinion motion conversion
model.description: Unqualified teaching proposal for human review: a bounded, prescribed pinion rotation drives signed rack travel through ideal continuous engagement.
assumptions: Illustrative adjustable defaults: commanded pinion angle 3.141592653589793 rad, pitch radius 0.04 m, elapsed time 0 s.
Supported input ranges: commanded pinion angle -6.28 to 6.28 rad; pitch radius 0.02 to 0.08 m; elapsed time 0 to 1 s.
The angle control specifies the final angular displacement from the common zero position. Play traverses that displacement uniformly over one second.
Coordinates: shaft along +z, rack travel along x, +y upward. Positive pinion angle is counterclockwise viewed from +z and moves the rack toward +x.
Initial conditions: pinion angular displacement and rack displacement are zero. Prescribed constant speed starts immediately and stops at the event end; acceleration is not modeled.
Rigid teeth, no slip and continuous engagement impose rack displacement = pitch radius × pinion angle.
Illustrative geometry: 20 pinion teeth; module = 2 × pitch radius / 20; rack pitch equals pinion circular pitch. Addendum is one module and dedendum is 1.25 modules.
Use a centered 1.4 m toothed rack and a guide covering the full supported travel. Rack displacement remains within ±0.5024 m, leaving end clearance.
Pinion center is fixed at the origin. Rack pitch line lies at y = -pitch radius; guide height follows the selected rack geometry.

Time experiment: input elapsed_time; step_seconds 0.01; playback_speed 1; reset_on_change [commanded_angle,pitch_radius]; end_time_id event_duration. Parameter changes atomically reset time; pause remains paused.
Angles use dimensionless radians; angle controls and readouts display degrees with display_scale 57.29577951308232.
Forward/reverse comparisons negate the commanded angle. Radius comparisons retain the same commanded angle and elapsed time. Existing snapshot comparison can retain the reference state.
limitations: This is a prescribed kinematic mechanism, not a dynamic simulation or engineering validation.
Backlash, friction, deformation, tooth stresses, torque and force prediction are excluded.
Tooth shapes are simplified teaching geometry with compatible pitch, not validated conjugate tooth profiles or a calculated contact solution.
Changing pitch radius represents a rescaled teaching assembly, not changing the radius of one manufactured gear.
The finite event does not model sustained rotation, acceleration, collision or rack-end disengagement. No external sources or manufacturer specifications are asserted.

nodes.description: Translation rate during playback; bounded [-0.5024,0.5024] m/s. Playback stops at the event end.

nodes.description: Pitch diameter divided by 20 teeth; range [0.002,0.008] m.

nodes.label: Pitch circumference
nodes.description: Distance traveled by the pitch circle in one revolution; range approximately [0.12566,0.50266] m.

nodes.label: Rack tooth spacing
nodes.description: Matching rack and pinion circular pitch; range approximately [0.006283,0.025133] m.

nodes.label: Pinion tooth-tip radius
nodes.description: Pitch radius plus one module; range [0.022,0.088] m.

nodes.label: Tooth root depth
nodes.description: Illustrative dedendum; range [0.0025,0.01] m.

nodes.label: Pinion tooth-root radius
nodes.description: Pitch radius minus dedendum; range [0.0175,0.07] m.

snapshot.unfinished_question: How does a rack and pinion turn rotation into straight-line movement?

definition.title: Rotation becomes straight-line travel
definition.description: A simplified teaching machine with an input wheel, toothed pinion, sliding rack and inspectable supports.

parts.label: Commanded pinion angle
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Final angle from zero; default 3.141592653589793 rad; range [-6.28,6.28]. Sign selects direction.

parts.label: Pinion pitch radius
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Adjustable illustrative radius; default 0.04 m; supported range [0.02,0.08] m.

parts.label: Current pinion angle
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Rotation about +z from the initial position; bounded [-6.28,6.28] rad.

parts.label: Signed rack displacement
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Rack translation along x from its initial centered position; bounded [-0.5024,0.5024] m.

parts.label: Elapsed time

parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Matching rack and pinion circular pitch; range approximately [0.006283,0.025133] m.

limits: Ideal rigid teeth, continuous engagement and no slip impose x=rθ, with θ in radians.
Positive rotation is counterclockwise viewed from +z and moves the rack toward +x. Shaft direction is +z; +y is up.
Backlash, friction, deformation, tooth stresses, torque, force prediction and engineering validation are excluded. Simplified teeth do not provide a contact solver.
Preserve the accepted angle range [-6.28,6.28] rad, radius range [0.02,0.08] m, one-second event and initial zero displacement.
The centered toothed rack stays 1.4 m long; travel remains bounded to ±0.5024 m. The long bed preserves these accepted quantities rather than shortening the rack for appearance.
Use 40 scene units per metre uniformly on all axes. Physical equations retain SI values.
Radius changes represent a reconfigured teaching assembly, not an adjustable manufactured gear. Matching tooth pitch, rack height and support apertures must change together.

Hardware dimensions and the large input handwheel are explicit teaching assumptions, not measured specifications or externally verified designs. The handwheel shares prescribed pinion rotation; no gearing or additional physics is implied by it, and its radius does not enter x=rθ. Its large diameter distinguishes input rotation from the small working pinion; offer a separate working-contact closeup

parts.label: Machine bed
parts.explanation: This thick bed supports the whole machine.

parts.label: Support wall
parts.explanation: This broad wall holds the shaft supports above the bed.

parts.label: Matching rotary assembly
parts.explanation: The pinion and its fitted supports change size together.

parts.label: Front bearing housing
parts.explanation: This bridge holds a bearing in front of the pinion.

parts.label: Front bearing
parts.explanation: Balls between open rings support the shaft while it turns.

parts.label: Rear bearing housing
parts.explanation: This housing keeps the rear shaft support aligned.

parts.label: Rear bearing
parts.explanation: This second bearing supports the long input shaft.

parts.label: Shared rotation
parts.explanation: The input wheel, shaft and pinion turn together.

parts.label: Drive shaft
parts.explanation: This shaft carries the input rotation to the pinion.

parts.label: Input handwheel
parts.explanation: This large wheel shows the rotary input clearly. It turns through the same angle as the pinion.

parts.label: Pinion hub
parts.explanation: This bored fitting joins the pinion to the shaft.

parts.label: Twenty-tooth pinion
parts.explanation: This round gear turns. Its teeth move the rack sideways.

parts.label: Shaft collars
parts.explanation: These rings keep the shaft from sliding through its bearings.

parts.label: Front bearing cap
parts.explanation: Remove this cap to inspect the front bearing.

parts.label: Rear bearing cap
parts.explanation: This removable ring holds the rear bearing in its housing.

parts.label: Guide height
parts.explanation: The guide follows the rack height when pinion size changes.

parts.label: Straight guide rails
parts.explanation: These rails keep the rack moving along one straight line.

parts.label: Guide liners
parts.explanation: These fitted strips form the surfaces the rack slides against.

parts.label: Rack travel
parts.explanation: The rack and its carrier slide together.

parts.label: Rack carrier
parts.explanation: This straight bar carries the toothed strip through the guide.

parts.label: Rack teeth
parts.explanation: These teeth match the pinion spacing. Their straight-line travel is the output.

parts.label: Sliding shoes
parts.explanation: These shaped edges fit inside the guide liners and keep the rack straight.

parts.label: Wall mounting fasteners
parts.explanation: These fasteners secure the wall feet to the bed.

parts.label: Bearing support fasteners
parts.explanation: These fasteners secure the bearing housings and their caps.

parts.label: Guide mounting fasteners
parts.explanation: These fasteners hold the guide feet on the bed.

experiments.title: Predict forward travel
experiments.prompt: Predict the rack direction for a positive half-turn. Set the angle, then play and inspect the pinion.
experiments.explanation: The pinion turns counterclockwise viewed from +z. Its matched teeth move the guided rack toward +x under the ideal no-slip law x=rθ.

experiments.title: Reverse the input
experiments.prompt: Keep the radius unchanged. Predict what reverses for a negative half-turn, then play and compare signed travel.
experiments.explanation: Reversing the pinion angle reverses rack displacement without changing its magnitude at the same radius and playback progress.

experiments.title: Try a smaller pinion
experiments.prompt: Keep the commanded angle unchanged. Predict travel with a 20 mm pitch radius, then play to the end and save a comparison.
experiments.explanation: The smaller pinion drives less rack travel at the same angle. Radius changes reconfigure the teaching assembly and matching tooth spacing.

experiments.title: Compare a larger pinion
experiments.prompt: Keep the same commanded angle. Predict travel with an 80 mm pitch radius, then play to the end and compare.
experiments.explanation: At the same angle, four times the pitch radius gives four times the signed travel. This prescribed kinematic model does not predict forces or tooth contact dynamics.

controls.help: Sets the final pinion angle from zero; positive rotation moves the rack toward +x, and changes restart playback time.
Rescales the teaching pinion and matching tooth spacing; a larger radius gives more travel at the same angle and restarts time.
Scrubs the one-second prescribed rotation and synchronized rack travel from their common zero positions.

time_experiment.explanation: From zero angle and displacement, θ=commanded_angle×elapsed_time/(1 s) and x=rθ. Prescribed uniform motion stops at one model second, shown over two screen seconds in slow motion; acceleration is not modeled. Parameter changes reset time atomically and preserve pause.

coverage.explanation: Inspect the rotating pinion and shaft, straight toothed rack and constraining guide. Inspection separation is not physical operating motion.
Inspect matched tooth spacing at the working contact. Synchronized motion illustrates ideal rigid teeth, continuous engagement and no slip; detailed contact and forces are not simulated.

Time and commanded angle determine current rotation; radius times that rotation determines signed rack travel. Radius also determines matching tooth pitch. Backlash, friction, deformation, stresses, torque and force prediction are excluded; this is not engineering validation.

outcomes: Identify the rotating pinion, straight toothed rack, and guide that constrains the rack to linear motion.
Explain how engagement between the pinion teeth and rack teeth transfers motion.
Observe how changing the pinion angle and rotation direction changes rack displacement, and how pitch radius affects travel for a given angle.

visual.scope: Eight fitted views; projected bounds, center-ray occlusion, conservative bounding-box overlaps and estimated two-line label capacity. These heuristics do not replace rendered-image or child usability review.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.
